title: Remove Invalid Parentheses - GeeksforGeeks
content:
Given a string s consisting of lowercase letters and parentheses '(' and ')'.

A string is considered valid if:

  • Every opening parenthesis '(' has a corresponding closing parenthesis ')'.
  • Parentheses are properly nested.

Remove the minimum number of invalid parentheses from s so that the resulting string becomes valid.  Return all the possible distinct valid strings in lexicographically sorted order.

Examples:

Input: s = "()())()"
Output: ["(())()", "()()()"]
Explanation: The string "()())()" has one extra ')', making it invalid. By removing one ')', we can make it valid in two ways:
Remove the 1st index ')' -> "(())()"
Remove the 4th index ')' -> "()()()"
Both are valid and require the minimum removals.

Input: s = "(a)())()"
Output: ["(a())()", "(a)()()"]
Explanation: We remove one ')' (minimum removals) to make it valid. Possible valid results:
Remove a ')' -> "(a())()"
Remove another ')' -> "(a)()()"

Input: s = ")("
Output: [""]
Explanation: The string ")(" is invalid. Removing both parentheses (minimum removals) gives an empty string "", which is valid.

Try It Yourself

Table of Content

  • Breadth First Search (BFS) - O(2 ^ n) Time and O(2 ^ n) Space
  • Depth First Search (DFS) - O(2 ^ n) Time and O(2 ^ n) Space

Breadth First Search (BFS) - O(2 ^ n) Time and O(2 ^ n) Space

The idea is to remove parentheses one by one and check whether the string is valid. BFS helps find the valid strings with the minimum removals.

  • Process strings level by level using a queue. At each level, we have one less character compared to the previous level.
  • Stop when a valid string is found and store all valid strings at that level.
  • Use a visited set to avoid duplicate strings.
C++ 
#include <bits/stdc++.h>
using namespace std;

// Check whether the given string has valid parentheses.
bool isValid(string s)
{
    int count = 0;

    // Traverse the string.
    for (char c : s)
    {

        // Increment for an opening parenthesis.
        if (c == '(')
            count++;

        // Decrement for a closing parenthesis.
        else if (c == ')')
        {
            count--;

            // More closing parentheses than opening ones.
            if (count < 0)
                return false;
        }
    }

    // Valid only when all opening parentheses are matched.
    return count == 0;
}

// Remove the minimum number of invalid parentheses.
vector<string> validParenthesis(string &s)
{

    // Store strings that have already been visited.
    unordered_set<string> visited;

    // Queue for BFS.
    queue<string> q;

    // Store all valid strings.
    vector<string> res;

    // Push the original string.
    q.push(s);

    // Mark the original string as visited.
    visited.insert(s);

    // Indicates that a valid string has been found.
    bool found = false;

    // Perform BFS.
    while (!q.empty())
    {

        // Get the current string.
        string curr = q.front();
        q.pop();

        // Check whether the current string is valid.
        if (isValid(curr))
        {
            res.push_back(curr);
            found = true;
        }

        // Do not generate the next level after
        // finding a valid string.
        if (found)
            continue;

        // Try removing each parenthesis.
        for (int i = 0; i < curr.length(); i++)
        {

            // Skip normal characters.
            if (curr[i] != '(' && curr[i] != ')')
                continue;

            // Remove the parenthesis at index i.
            string next = curr.substr(0, i) + curr.substr(i + 1);

            // Process only unvisited strings.
            if (visited.find(next) == visited.end())
            {
                visited.insert(next);
                q.push(next);
            }
        }
    }

    // Sort the valid strings lexicographically.
    sort(res.begin(), res.end());

    return res;
}

int main()
{

    string s = "(a)())()";

    vector<string> res = validParenthesis(s);

    cout << "[";

    for (int i = 0; i < res.size(); i++)
    {

        if (i > 0)
            cout << ", ";

        cout << "\"" << res[i] << "\"";
    }

    cout << "]";

    return 0;
}

        // Queue for BFS.

        // Store all valid strings.

        q.Enqueue(s);

        // Mark the original string as visited.
        visited.Add(s);

        bool found = false;

        while (q.Count > 0) {

            string curr = q.Dequeue();

            // Check whether the current string is valid.
            if (IsValid(curr)) {
                res.Add(curr);
                found = true;

            if (found)

            // Try removing each parenthesis.
            for (int i = 0; i < curr.Length; i++) {
                // Skip normal characters.
                if (curr[i] != '(' && curr[i] != ')')
                    continue;

                // Remove the parenthesis at index i.
                string next = curr.Substring(0, i)
                              + curr.Substring(i + 1);

                // Process only unvisited strings.
                if (!visited.Contains(next)) {
                    visited.Add(next);
                    q.Enqueue(next);
                }
            }
        }

        // Sort the valid strings lexicographically.
        res.Sort();

        return res;
    }

    {

        List<string> res = obj.validParenthesis(s);

Depth First Search (DFS) - O(2 ^ n) Time and O(2 ^ n) Space

The idea is to first find how many ( and ) need to be removed. Then use DFS to try keeping or removing parentheses while maintaining a valid balance.

  • Find the number of invalid ( and ) to remove.
  • Use recursion to keep or remove each parenthesis and maintain the balance.
  • Store the strings that end with balance 0 and use a set to avoid duplicates.

Let us understand with an example:
Input: s = "(a)())()"

  • Count invalid parentheses: open = 0, close = 1.
  • Start recursion with index = 0, open = 0, close = 1, pair = 0, cur = "".
  • At index = 0, keep ( -> pair = 1, cur = "(".
  • At index = 1, keep a -> cur = "(a".
  • At index = 2, keep ) -> pair = 0, cur = "(a)".
  • At index = 3, keep ( -> pair = 1, cur = "(a)(".
  • At index = 4, keep ) -> pair = 0, cur = "(a)()".
  • At index = 5, ) cannot be kept because pair = 0, so remove it.
  • Continue with the remaining (), keeping both parentheses -> cur = "(a)()()".
  • In another recursion path, remove the ) at index = 2 and keep the remaining parentheses -> cur = "(a())()".
  • At the end, strings are added only when open = 0, close = 0, and pair = 0.
  • Therefore, the distinct valid results are: ["(a())()", "(a)()()"].
C++ 
#include <bits/stdc++.h>
using namespace std;

// Recursive function to find all valid strings.
void findValid(string str, int index, int open, int close, int pair, string cur, vector<string> &res,
               unordered_set<string> &st)
{
    // If the end of the string is reached.
    if (index == str.size())
    {
        // Check if all invalid parentheses are removed
        // and no unmatched opening parenthesis is left.
        if (open == 0 && close == 0 && pair == 0)
        {
            // Add only distinct strings.
            if (st.find(cur) == st.end())
            {
                res.push_back(cur);
                st.insert(cur);
            }
        }

        return;
    }

    // If the current character is not a parenthesis.
    if (str[index] != '(' && str[index] != ')')
    {
        // Keep the character.
        findValid(str, index + 1, open, close, pair, cur + str[index], res, st);
    }
    else
    {
        // If the current character is an opening parenthesis.
        if (str[index] == '(')
        {
            // Remove the current parenthesis.
            if (open > 0)
            {
                findValid(str, index + 1, open - 1, close, pair, cur, res, st);
            }

            // Keep the current parenthesis.
            findValid(str, index + 1, open, close, pair + 1, cur + str[index], res, st);
        }
        else
        {
            // Remove the current parenthesis.
            if (close > 0)
            {
                findValid(str, index + 1, open, close - 1, pair, cur, res, st);
            }

            // Keep the current parenthesis if it has
            // a matching opening parenthesis.
            if (pair > 0)
            {
                findValid(str, index + 1, open, close, pair - 1, cur + str[index], res, st);
            }
        }
    }
}

vector<string> validParenthesis(string &str)
{
    vector<string> result;
    unordered_set<string> st;

    // Count invalid opening and closing parentheses.
    int open = 0, close = 0;

    // Find the minimum parentheses to remove.
    for (char c : str)
    {
        // Count opening parentheses.
        if (c == '(')
            open++;

        // Match a closing parenthesis with an opening one.
        else if (c == ')')
        {
            if (open != 0)
                open--;
            else
                close++;
        }
    }

    // Generate all valid strings.
    findValid(str, 0, open, close, 0, "", result, st);

    // Sort the result lexicographically.
    sort(result.begin(), result.end());

    return result;
}

function findValid(str, index, open, close, pair, cur, res,
                   st)
{
    // If the end of the string is reached.
    if (index === str.length) {
        // Check if all invalid parentheses are removed
        // and no unmatched opening parenthesis is left.
        if (open === 0 && close === 0 && pair === 0) {
            // Add only distinct strings.
            if (!st.has(cur)) {
                res.push(cur);
                st.add(cur);
            }
        }

        return;
    }

    // If the current character is not a parenthesis.
    if (str[index] !== "(" && str[index] !== ")") {
        // Keep the character.
        findValid(str, index + 1, open, close, pair,
                  cur + str[index], res, st);
    }
    else {
        // If the current character is an opening
        // parenthesis.
        if (str[index] === "(") {
            // Remove the current parenthesis.
            if (open > 0) {
                findValid(str, index + 1, open - 1, close,
                          pair, cur, res, st);
            }

            // Keep the current parenthesis.
            findValid(str, index + 1, open, close, pair + 1,
                      cur + str[index], res, st);
        }
        else {
            // Remove the current parenthesis.
            if (close > 0) {
                findValid(str, index + 1, open, close - 1,
                          pair, cur, res, st);
            }

            // Keep the current parenthesis if it has
            // a matching opening parenthesis.
            if (pair > 0) {
                findValid(str, index + 1, open, close,
                          pair - 1, cur + str[index], res,
                          st);
            }
        }
    }
}

function validParenthesis(str)
{
    let result = [];
    let st = new Set();

    // Count invalid opening and closing parentheses.
    let open = 0, close = 0;

    // Find the minimum parentheses to remove.
    for (let c of str) {
        // Count opening parentheses.
        if (c === "(") {
            open++;
            // Match a closing parenthesis with an opening
            // one.
        }
        else if (c === ")") {
            if (open !== 0) {
                open--;
            }
            else {
                close++;
            }
        }
    }

    // Generate all valid strings.
    findValid(str, 0, open, close, 0, "", result, st);

    // Sort the result lexicographically.
    result.sort();

    return result;
}
